title: Foundations: Ska - The Complete Guide
summary: What Ska is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Ska songs: Ska is Jamaica's original pop: jazz horns, walking bass, and guitar chopping fast offbeats at 1960s dance halls. It became England's 2 Tone movement in 1979 and America's third wave in the 1990s.

History: The Skatalites (1964) defined first-wave ska; the Specials and Madness led the 2 Tone revival; No Doubt and Sublime carried third wave in the 1990s.

How the songs work: Ska favors the keys of C, G, F, Bb. Common forms include Verse-chorus at double-time feel; Horn-section riffs as hooks. Players should master upstroke guitar chops on every offbeat first, then walking bass under horn stabs. Bright, fast, upstroke-driven.
